references.text: Judas was in charge of the money bag and stole from it, which establishes his role as treasurer and his greed before he is told to act in 13:29.
Jesus gives Judas a direct instruction ("What you are going to do, do quickly"), which the disciples misunderstand as an order to buy something with the money, just as in 13:29.
Immediately after the disciples think Jesus has sent Judas to make a purchase, Judas leaves the feast, confirming that the misunderstanding in 13:29 was based on his mission.
Judas negotiates the price for betraying Jesus, showing that his actions regarding money and the money bag in the Gospel of John were driven by greed.
